To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) adversarially robust neural networks are regularized towards solutions of lower confidence by making feature changes induced by perturbations in instance space smoother uniformly in all direction; and (2) this regularizer is the reason for the performance degradation on natural data.

(1) adversarial robustness is achieved through regularization; (2) the regularization is achieved by making changes in the feature spaces of most layers smoother in all directions; (3) such smoothing leads to worse performance on natural examples; (4) the regularization is not necessary to build robustness into NNs, and one can consider other methods that are more friendly to standard performance.

adversarial robustness is achieved by regularizations that make the changes in the features space of most layers smoother, and that such regularization concentrates samples around decision boundary, resulting in less confidence in the prediction, which leads to standard performance degradation.
